description: PR drops the first element ('exports') of a count-indexed bucket list in terraform.tfvars (plus an Owner default tag, and pipeline log retention 30 -> 14 days: acceptable, a retention cut). Every later index shifts, so four data buckets are renamed (replaced) and the last is destroyed: the classic count re-index data loss.

material.why: Removing 'exports' from the front of data_buckets shifts every count index: this bucket's name changes (acme-prod-exports -> acme-prod-invoices), and a bucket name forces replacement, so the plan destroys the existing versioned bucket and creates an empty one. force_destroy is false, so the destroy fails on a non-empty bucket (BucketNotEmpty) and the apply stops partway; emptying it or setting force_destroy to get past that loses every object.

Removing 'exports' from the front of data_buckets shifts every count index: this bucket's name changes (acme-prod-invoices -> acme-prod-receipts), and a bucket name forces replacement, so the plan destroys the existing versioned bucket and creates an empty one. force_destroy is false, so the destroy fails on a non-empty bucket (BucketNotEmpty) and the apply stops partway; emptying it or setting force_destroy to get past that loses every object.

Removing 'exports' from the front of data_buckets shifts every count index: this bucket's name changes (acme-prod-receipts -> acme-prod-statements), and a bucket name forces replacement, so the plan destroys the existing versioned bucket and creates an empty one. force_destroy is false, so the destroy fails on a non-empty bucket (BucketNotEmpty) and the apply stops partway; emptying it or setting force_destroy to get past that loses every object.

Removing 'exports' from the front of data_buckets shifts every count index: this bucket's name changes (acme-prod-statements -> acme-prod-ledger), and a bucket name forces replacement, so the plan destroys the existing versioned bucket and creates an empty one. force_destroy is false, so the destroy fails on a non-empty bucket (BucketNotEmpty) and the apply stops partway; emptying it or setting force_destroy to get past that loses every object.

The list is one element shorter, so index [4] (acme-prod-ledger) is out of range and is destroyed (with force_destroy false the destroy fails while the bucket holds objects; emptying it to proceed loses them); the 'ledger' dataset moves to index [3], which renames (replaces) acme-prod-statements. The PR meant to drop 'exports' but actually deletes or recreates all five buckets.
